findings.title: isAccessTokenId matcher uses wrong offset and inverted condition, so it never checks the grant
findings.body: The grant shortcut sits at indices 4–6 of the prefix (e.g. "onrtac"), but the matcher reads `substring(3, 5)`, which gives "ta" for "onrtac". The condition is also inverted: it returns false when the substring *equals* the expected shortcut. Together this means the grant-type check practically always passes. The new assertions in expectCodeToToken, expectRefresh, expectDeviceCodeToToken and expectAuthReqIdToToken therefore do not verify which grant produced the token. It should be `if (!items[0].substring(4, 6).equals(expectedGrantShortcut)) return false;`, ideally with a length check first.

findings.title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant type factories
findings.body: `getShortcut()` is added to the public OAuth2GrantTypeFactory SPI with no default implementation. Existing third-party grant type factories will no longer compile. Already-compiled ones will throw AbstractMethodError in DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit when it calls `gtf.getShortcut()` during startup. If an implementation returns null, `ConcurrentHashMap.put(null, ...)` throws NPE and also aborts startup. A default method (e.g. derived from the id or returning a fallback) and null handling are needed.

findings.title: Decoder hard-codes 2-character shortcuts while the SPI contract suggests 3-letter ones
findings.body: The OAuth2GrantTypeFactory javadoc says the shortcut is "usually like 3-letters", and no length is enforced anywhere. The encoder concatenates whatever shortcut a factory returns, but `getTokenContextFromTokenId` rejects any prefix that is not exactly 6 characters and splits it at fixed 2-char offsets. A custom grant with a 3-letter shortcut will issue tokens whose IDs cannot later be decoded and throw IllegalArgumentException. Either validate that shortcuts are exactly 2 chars at registration and fix the javadoc, or use a delimiter-based format.

findings.title: Public copy constructor of OAuth2GrantType.Context removed
findings.body: The public `Context(Context context)` copy constructor was deleted from a public SPI class. Any extension or internal code that wraps or copies the grant context with it will no longer compile. If a copy constructor is still wanted, it should be kept and also copy the new `grantType` field.

findings.title: rawTokenId null-check validates grantType instead
findings.body: `Objects.requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed")` checks grantType a second time, so a null rawTokenId is accepted silently. Encoding would then produce IDs like "onrtac:null". It should be `Objects.requireNonNull(rawTokenId, ...)`.

findings.title: Lightweight-token detection now runs for every access token and can NPE without a context client
findings.body: `initToken` now calls `AbstractOIDCProtocolMapper.getShouldUseLightweightToken(session)` for every access token. That method dereferences `session.getContext().getClient()` without a null check. Before, it was only reached from mapper code. Any code path that creates access tokens while the KeycloakSession context has no client set will now fail with NullPointerException. Consider using `clientSessionContext.getClientSession().getClient()` instead.

findings.title: Lazy refresh of grant maps skips duplicate-shortcut validation
findings.body: postInit checks that no two grants share a shortcut. The runtime refresh paths in getShortcutByGrantType and getGrantTypeByShortcut just `put` into both maps. A grant deployed later with a colliding shortcut silently overwrites the existing shortcut→grant mapping, so later decoding returns the wrong grant type for tokens issued by the original grant.

findings.title: testIncorrectGrantType passes because of an NPE, not the intended validation
findings.body: The factory in this test has a null sessionFactory. An unknown shortcut makes getGrantTypeByShortcut call `sessionFactory.getProviderFactoriesStream(...)`, which throws NullPointerException. Catching `RuntimeException` hides this, so the test never exercises the intended "Unknown value ... for grant type" IllegalArgumentException. It should catch IllegalArgumentException and mock or stub the session factory.
